docs.title: Servo Motor Explanation
docs.text:
A servo motor is a type of motor designed for precise control of angular or linear position, velocity, and acceleration. It operates as part of a closed-loop control system that constantly monitors and adjusts its motion to achieve accurate positioning.

  1. Basic Concept

A servo motor system consists of:

A motor (DC or AC)

A feedback device (encoder or potentiometer)

A control circuit (servo controller or driver)

The feedback device continuously measures the motor’s position, and the control circuit adjusts the motor’s movement to match the desired value.

  1. Working Principle

An input signal specifies the desired position.

The controller compares this input with the feedback signal from the sensor.

The error signal (difference between desired and actual position) is generated.

The controller drives the motor to correct the error.

The motor stops when the error reaches zero.

This process is called closed-loop control, as it constantly checks and corrects the position.

  1. Main Components
Component Function Motor Provides the mechanical motion. Gearbox Reduces speed and increases torque. Feedback Sensor Measures shaft position and provides feedback. Control Circuit Compares input and feedback signals and drives the motor accordingly.
